images.title: Even or odd number of negative factors
images.purpose: Compares (−2)⁴ = 16, where all negative factors pair up, with (−4)³ = −64, where one factor is left without a partner.
images.composition: Plain white background, lots of empty space around the main object, no scenery, no people, no extra text. Two rows of factor tiles, one above the other, each followed by its value on the right.
images.exact_structure: Top row: exactly 4 equal square vermilion (#D55E00) tiles in a line, each showing '−2'. Under the tiles, 2 green (#009E73) brackets, one under tiles 1 and 2 and one under tiles 3 and 4. At the right end of the row, the value '16' and the label 'even count' under it. Bottom row: exactly 3 equal square vermilion (#D55E00) tiles in a line, each showing '−4'. One green (#009E73) bracket under tiles 1 and 2; tile 3 has no bracket and is circled with a thick vermilion (#D55E00) ring. At the right end of the row, the value '−64' and the label 'odd count' under it. All minus signs are true minus signs, not hyphens. Exactly 7 tiles, 3 brackets, 1 ring.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: An even number of negative factors gives a positive value; an odd number gives a negative value.
images.description: Compares (−2)⁴ = 16, where all negative factors pair up, with (−4)³ = −64, where one factor is left without a partner.
images.context: (−2)⁴ = 16 and (−4)³ = −64. Each bracketed pair of negatives multiplies to a positive.
images.teaching_notes: Labels '−2' (4 times) and '−4' (3 times) are drawn on every tile. Extend: (−1) to the power 56 is 1, (−1) to the power 5 is −1, and powers of 0 are 0.

image_decisions.why: Pairing negative factors shows why the sign depends on whether the count is even or odd, which is this concept.
